newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks push higher at open, NYSE sets curbs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks push higher at open, NYSE sets curbs.

text.p: U.S. stocks made a swift push higher on Wednesday morning, extending exuberant gains after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's upbeat Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on the economy yesterday.
The Dow Jones Industrial average quickly climbed 71 points, or 0.88 percent, to 8132.
The New York Stock Exchange set index-arbitrage trading curbs nine minutes after the open.
The Nasdaq composite also powered upwards, rising around 13 points, or 0.84 percent, to 1577.

"This market just doesn't want to quit," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co, said. "The money flows into equities, essentially into blue chip stocks. We are seeing a blue chip buying binge."
The long bond was slightly firmer, trading up 1/32 to yield 6.41 percent.
Boeing Co stock surged in active trade, after the European Commission recommended approval of a planned $15 billion merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.
